NoData hole
A patch with no image data inside the area. Users see a black hole; anything underneath cannot be mapped.
Cloud cover
Cloud or haze hides the ground. Features under it cannot be mapped or checked.
Colour jump between tiles
Neighbouring tiles or scenes have different colour balance, so the same surface looks different and a visible line appears.
Seamline through a building
The join between two scenes cuts a building, so its two halves do not line up.
Leaning building
A tall building leans away from its footprint because it was not fully orthorectified. The roof sits away from where the walls meet the ground.
Void
Cells with no height value, usually over water, shadows or dense vegetation where matching failed.
Step at tile edge
Heights jump where two tiles meet, creating a false cliff.
Spike
A single cell far higher than its neighbours, usually a matching error.
Pit
A single cell far lower than its neighbours. It can trap water in flow models.
Bridge left in the DTM
The bridge deck stays in the bare-earth model and acts like a dam across the river.
Lake not flat
The water surface should be one height; noise makes it rise and fall.
Overlapping buildings
Two building polygons share area, so areas and counts are wrong.
Undershoot (dangle)
A road stops just short of the road it should join, breaking the network for routing.
Overshoot
A road continues past the junction it should end at.
Gap or sliver
A thin empty strip between polygons that should share a boundary.
Self-intersection
A polygon crosses itself, so its area and shape are invalid.
Duplicate feature
The same feature captured twice, so counts and statistics are inflated.
Omission
A building visible in the image was not captured.
Wrong classification
The feature is captured but given the wrong class, for example a dirt track recorded as a primary road.
Displaced feature
The outline does not sit on the real object in the image.
Salt-and-pepper noise
Isolated pixels of a different class, smaller than the minimum mapping unit.
Misclassified surface
A surface given an impossible class, for example a dark roof labelled as water.
Completeness
Is everything that should be there present, and nothing extra?
Real-world items missing from the data.
A building visible in the orthoimage but not digitised; a void in a DEM.
Commission
Items in the data that should not be there.
A demolished building still in the data; a duplicate road.
Logical consistency
Does the data obey its own rules?
Conceptual consistency
Data follows the conceptual schema (feature types, relationships).
A water line stored in the roads feature class.
Domain consistency
Values fall within allowed lists or ranges.
A road class code not in the domain; a land cover code not in the legend.
Format consistency
Data is stored in the specified physical structure.
A 16-bit tile in an 8-bit delivery; wrong CRS on one layer.
Topological consistency
Geometric relationships are correct.
Overlapping buildings, road dangles, polygon gaps.
Is each thing in the right place?
Absolute (external)
Closeness of coordinates to true positions.
Building corners vs GNSS check points: RMSE, CE90.
Relative (internal)
Correct positions of features relative to each other.
Straight walls and right angles kept; edges match across tiles.
Gridded data positional accuracy
Closeness of grid cell positions to true positions.
Ortho or DEM check points: CE90, LE90.
Is each thing correctly described?
Classification correctness
Items assigned to the right class.
Land cover confusion matrix; a track recorded as a primary road.
Non-quantitative attribute correctness
Descriptive attributes are right.
Wrong surface type or road name.
Quantitative attribute accuracy
Numeric attributes are close to true values.
DEM heights, building heights, road widths.

Recorded dates are correct.
Wrong acquisition date in the ortho metadata.

Demolition date before construction date.
